html:
Maravi was a group of Chewa kingdoms around the southern end of Lake Malawi, founded around 1500 and strongest in the early 17th century; the country of Malawi takes its name from it.

Its paramount ruler, the Kalonga, and allied chiefs such as Lundu and Undi controlled the land between the lake and the Zambezi. They traded ivory and iron with the Portuguese at Tete and Sena, and around 1600 Maravi warriors fought as far as the Mozambique coast.

The kingdoms broke up in the 18th century, and Ngoni and Yao invaders struck the region in the 19th. Chewa institutions such as the Gule Wamkulu masked dances survive, and the Chewa are still the largest people of Malawi, neighbours of the Yao.
sum: Maravi was a group of Chewa kingdoms around the southern end of Lake Malawi, founded around 1500 and strongest in the early 17th century; the country of Malawi takes its name from it.
